newsitem.title: UKRAINE: New Ukraine PM promises to pay off wage debt.
newsitem.headline: New Ukraine PM promises to pay off wage debt.

text.p: Ukrainian Prime Minister Valery Pustovoitenko said on Monday his government would try to pay off a huge backlog of unpaid wages in the former Soviet republic within four months.

"The main issue in preventing a crisis is the payment of wages and pensions. We have prepared a government resolution how we can do this," Pustovoitenko told a news conference alongside visiting Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene
"There is also a presidential decree which obliges us to pay off all debts by December 1 and we are dealing with this. The problem must be resolved," added the premier, who was appointed in mid-July.
Official statistics estimate the backlog in unpaid wages, pensions and student grants at 6.7 billlion hryvnias ($3.6 billion).

Analysts estimate 12 million people are affected by delays -- almost one in three Ukrainians of working age -- provoking sporadic strikes and rallies by some workers, including large protests by coal miners recently.
President Leonid Kuchma, trying to speed up economic reforms, reshuffled his cabinet on Friday. Pustovoitenko said a final round of appointments was due on Tuesday.
Former prime minister Pavlo Lazarenko, who resigned this month, promised to solve the unpaid wage crisis by September last year. He had taken office four months before.
